record.original_question: Is every non-trivial (a, b)-geproci set forced to contain three collinear points, or can one construct a counterexample?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.7. Prove or disprove (by giving a counterexample) that every non-trivial (a, b)-geproci set has a subset of 3 collinear points.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in projective space $\mathbb{P}^3$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. A finite set of points $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ is said to have the geproci property if there exist integers $a\le b$ such that, for a general plane $H\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ and a general point $p\in\mathbb{P}^3$, the projection of $Z$ from $p$ to $H$ is a complete intersection in $H\cong\mathbb{P}^2$ of two plane curves of degrees $a$ and $b$ (necessarily with $|Z|=ab$); in this case $Z$ is called an $(a,b)$-geproci set. The set $Z$ is called trivial if it is contained in a plane (equivalently, if $a=1$). 

Question: Does every non-trivial $(a,b)$-geproci set $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ contain three collinear points? Either prove that any such $Z$ must contain a subset of three collinear points, or exhibit a non-trivial $(a,b)$-geproci set containing no three collinear points.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on geproci sets (2023–2024) on arXiv discuss the classification of $(a,b)$-geproci sets, the half-grid and non-half-grid examples (smallest non-grid example has 12 points of type $(3,4)$; the $H_4$ 60-point set, etc.). The question of whether every non-trivial geproci set must contain three collinear points is posed as an open problem in this body of work; no proof or counterexample was located in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Geproci sets and the combinatorics of skew lines in P^3
status_evidence.snippet: Studies (a,b)-geproci sets and collinearity structure on skew lines, listing open problems about combinatorial constraints.
status_evidence.claim: The problem about forced 3-collinear subsets in non-trivial geproci sets is discussed but not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Geproci sets on skew lines in P^3 with two transversals
status_evidence.snippet: Examines collinearities arising in known non-trivial geproci configurations such as the (3,4) 12-point set and the H_4 60-point set.
status_evidence.claim: All known non-trivial geproci examples have 3 collinear points, but no general proof or counterexample is given.
